solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Prisoner inspired by state of belonging, finally (2,10)

indicatorNotes.inspired by: to be inspired is to be breathed in, so the prisoner goes inside

blocks.note: inclusion is the state of belonging to a group

annotation.surface: A convict takes heart from finally feeling he belongs somewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: CON slips in after the first two letters of INCLUSION.
annotation.definitionFit: 'In conclusion' is how a speaker says 'finally'.

entries.clue: Prehistoric period over, about which I seethe (4,3)

indicatorNotes.about which: the words that follow go round the word before

annotation.surface: Someone fuming that a prehistoric era is over and done with.
annotation.walkthrough: ON sits between the R and the A of I RAGE.
annotation.definitionFit: Archaeologists name prehistoric eras by their tools, and the era when iron replaced bronze is the Iron Age.

entries.clue: Made chess move, guided by players? (7)

blocks.note: the cast is the players in a show

annotation.surface: A chess player whose moves were steered by teammates.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'guided by players' backwards: the players (CAST) come first, then LED. 'Players' pulls towards chess players, but it means actors.
annotation.definitionFit: To castle is a chess move swapping king and rook.

entries.clue: A nice rum shot left – on the counter? (9)

indicatorNotes.shot: shot as in wrecked, ruined: the letters are knocked out of order

annotation.surface: A drink of rum left sitting on the bar counter.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts the rum on a bar counter; the definition means a counting device, where everything is expressed in numbers.
annotation.definitionFit: Something on a counter (a meter or tally) is shown in numbers, so numerical.

entries.clue: Enjoy young animal from California? (3,2)

blocks.note: LA = Los Angeles, a city in California
a pup is a young dog or seal

annotation.surface: A request to enjoy a baby animal from California.
annotation.walkthrough: The Californian young animal is an 'LA pup'.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom from a cat at a saucer: lapping up praise means relishing it.

entries.clue: Lawmaker in refinement of one’s art (7)

indicatorNotes.refinement of: refining something reworks it into a new form

annotation.surface: A legislator busy polishing their own craft.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'one’s' is ignored; only the seven letters count.
annotation.definitionFit: A senator sits in a senate and makes laws.

entries.clue: Capital in instant raised before newspaper folding (7)

indicatorNotes.in: being in something means sitting inside it, so the capital sits inside the instant
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raised means read upwards
indicatorNotes.before: puts that result ahead of the newspaper

blocks.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
the i is a British newspaper

annotation.surface: Folding up the newspaper in a hurry.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the instant is raised; the capital then sits inside it. The i is a British national daily, a favourite one-letter newspaper in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding.

entries.clue: How to catch river’s salmon for bird (5,7)

indicatorNotes.to catch: to catch something is to trap it, so HOW holds the rest inside

blocks.note: the word itself, split round the rest
the Ouse is an English river, plus the S of the possessive
a parr is a young salmon

annotation.surface: Advice on landing a salmon from a river, oddly aimed at a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: The fishing picture makes 'How' a question word; it is simply the outer letters, and the catch goes inside it. The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, another in Sussex.
annotation.definitionFit: Defined by its class: the house sparrow is the familiar brown bird that nests round buildings.

entries.clue: Marsupial with problem tracking spoor that’s been cut off (7)

indicatorNotes.cut: to cut a word short is to trim its tail, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.off: off as in bad, gone wrong: the letters are mixed
indicatorNotes.tracking: following, so the problem comes after

blocks.note: SPOOR without its R is SPOO, then rearranged
a sum is an arithmetic problem

annotation.surface: A hunter following an animal's trail until the tracks run out.
annotation.walkthrough: Spoor is the trail of an animal, which suits the hunting surface. Its letters are trimmed then jumbled before SUM follows.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the opossum carries its young in a pouch, so it is a marsupial, the only kind native to the Americas outside the far south.

entries.clue: Innocent, perhaps, plea initially working before argument (7)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the start of plea is used
indicatorNotes.before: places the working part ahead of the argument

blocks.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel

annotation.surface: A defendant who is innocent pleading before the legal argument starts.
annotation.walkthrough: Innocent here is a name, not a verdict: thirteen popes took the name Innocent.
annotation.definitionFit: A pontiff is a pope, and Innocent is one papal name.

entries.clue: Denial of talent brought home to farm animals, performing fleas way ahead! (5,7)

indicatorNotes.performing: the fleas perform tricks, so their letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.ahead: the anagram and the way go in front of the home

blocks.note: a mode is a way of doing something
a sty is where pigs live

annotation.surface: A flea circus promoter modestly playing down their act while boasting it beats the farmyard.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads in reverse of the clue: FALSE and MODE go ahead of STY.
annotation.definitionFit: False modesty is pretending you lack talent you know you have.

entries.clue: Page with less original outline – device bringing documents together? (7)

indicatorNotes.outline: the outer word forms an outline round the page

annotation.surface: An office scene: a page, a stale outline and a gadget for binding papers.
annotation.walkthrough: P sits inside STALER, which gives the page its outline.
annotation.definitionFit: A stapler fastens sheets of paper together.

entries.clue: Banana skin with fat bananas in something bitter to swallow? (7)

indicatorNotes.bananas: bananas = crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: a pill, as in a bitter pill to swallow

annotation.surface: Someone forcing down a mashed-up banana skin with some fat.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is full of bananas, but 'bananas' is only the mixing signal; the definition is the other banana, a banana skin being a hidden hazard.
annotation.definitionFit: A banana skin is British slang for an unforeseen trap, which is a pitfall.

entries.clue: Beginning on spaghetti, hang on … fork out! (5)

indicatorNotes.Beginning on: take the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: to pend is to hang, awaiting a decision

annotation.surface: A diner about to twirl spaghetti on a fork, told to wait.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'fork' cutlery; 'fork out' means pay up.
annotation.definitionFit: To fork out is to spend money, usually reluctantly.

entries.clue: Characteristic of chicken, animal I cared about (9)

annotation.surface: A farmer describing the animals they looked after, chickens included.
annotation.walkthrough: Chicken here is a person too scared to act, not a bird, so the farmyard surface misleads.
annotation.definitionFit: Being chicken means being cowardly, and cowardice is that quality.

entries.clue: Bore accompanying rose (9)

annotation.surface: A dull person turning up with a flower.
annotation.walkthrough: Bore is the past tense of bear, not a dull person, and rose is the past tense of rise, not a flower.
annotation.definitionFit: To bear hardship is to withstand it, so bore = withstood.

entries.clue: Drive past car in unconscious state (9)

indicatorNotes.past: the driving part comes past, after, the car

blocks.note: to pilot is to drive or steer

annotation.surface: A driver passing a car while barely awake.
annotation.walkthrough: Doing something on autopilot means doing it without conscious thought.
annotation.definitionFit: Autopilot is the state of acting without thinking.

entries.clue: Scene where Greek character keeps fit (7)

indicatorNotes.keeps: the Greek letter keeps the other word inside it

annotation.surface: A setting where a Greek person stays in shape.
annotation.walkthrough: Character means a letter here, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French for 'picture': a tableau is a striking arranged scene, as on a stage.

entries.clue: Best time to plant additional mint, say (7)

indicatorNotes.to plant: the best time has something planted inside it

blocks.note: a PB is a personal best, an athlete's best time

annotation.surface: Gardening advice on when to put in more mint.
annotation.walkthrough: The gardening surface wants 'best time to plant' to be a season; it is PB, a personal best, with OTHER planted in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A potherb is a herb grown for cooking, and mint is one.

entries.clue: First notes written in print, romanticised (5)

indicatorNotes.written in: the answer is written inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A romance's opening lines appear in print.
annotation.walkthrough: Notes are musical notes: the first notes of a song are its intro.
annotation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a piece of music.

entries.clue: Reworked routine – as yet undelivered? (2,5)

indicatorNotes.Reworked: reworking the word rearranges its letters

annotation.surface: A revised routine that has not been presented yet.
annotation.walkthrough: Undelivered sounds like post or a speech; here it is a baby not yet born.
annotation.definitionFit: A baby in utero is still in the womb, not yet delivered.

entries.clue: Young English horse accessing area on course (7)

indicatorNotes.accessing: getting into, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: a tee is the area on a golf course where each hole starts
a nag is an old horse

annotation.surface: A young English horse getting onto the racecourse.
annotation.walkthrough: The course is a golf course, not a racecourse: E NAG goes inside TEE.
annotation.definitionFit: Teenage means in one's teens, so young.

entries.clue: Steal, and sound emotionless (7)

blocks.note: otic means relating to the ear, so to do with sound

annotation.surface: A thief keeping a flat voice during a robbery.
annotation.walkthrough: Otic is a medical word meaning 'of the ear'.
annotation.definitionFit: Robotic describes someone mechanical and without feeling.

entries.clue: Country of New Guinea first of all leading a dance (5)

indicatorNotes.first of all: take the first letter of each word
indicatorNotes.leading: those letters come ahead of the A

blocks.clueFragment: Country of New Guinea first of all
blocks.note: first letters of Country Of New Guinea

annotation.surface: A New Guinea native at the head of a dance line.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Papua New Guinea; the first letters only nearly spell CONGO.
annotation.definitionFit: The conga is a dance performed in a long line.

entries.clue: Beloved stuff (7)

blocks.note: informal noun for a sweetheart, as in 'main ...'
a verb here: to cram something in tightly

annotation.surface: Affectionate talk about treasured belongings.
annotation.walkthrough: Stuff reads as a noun, possessions, but works as the verb to cram.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang for a partner ('main squeeze'), and a plain synonym for cramming things in.

entries.clue: How bag stuffed with present (7)

indicatorNotes.stuffed with: the bag word is filled with the next

blocks.note: to bag a prize is to win it
here = present, as at a roll call

annotation.surface: A puzzled question about how a bag got so full of a gift.
annotation.walkthrough: Bag is a verb, to win, not a sack; present means in attendance, not a gift.
annotation.definitionFit: Wherein means in what way or respect, so how.

entries.clue: Ham, tricky to carve (7)

indicatorNotes.tricky: the letters play tricks, rearranging themselves

annotation.surface: A joint of ham that is awkward to slice.
annotation.walkthrough: The ham on the carving board is really the verb for a bad actor's excess.
annotation.definitionFit: Theatre slang: a ham is a showy actor, so to ham it up is to overact.

entries.clue: Insincere feeling within the Cabinet? (8,4)

blocks.note: the straight sense: affection faked for gain
the surface means the government Cabinet; the setter means a cabinet in the kitchen, a storage unit

annotation.surface: Government ministers pretending to like each other.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C makes it the political Cabinet; read it as a kitchen cabinet and the feeling kept inside it is cupboard love.
annotation.definitionFit: Cupboard love is affection shown only to get something, as a pet fawns for food.
